description: Comprehensive demo documentation package: video walkthrough script with timestamps, public tunnel setup guide, 5-minute live demo script, pitch deck (Markdown), enhanced README sections, and GitHub repository polish.
steps: Create docs/video-walkthrough-script.md with detailed 8-10 minute video script. Structure: 1) Introduction (0:00-0:45, problem statement: manual API migration toil), 2) Product Overview (0:45-1:30, autonomous pipeline diagram), 3) Architecture Deep Dive (1:30-3:00, show apps/api/, packages/, database schema in Neon console), 4) Live Demo Part 1 (3:00-5:00, start backend and frontend, walk through Dashboard showing pipeline steps and activity feed), 5) Live Demo Part 2 (5:00-7:00, trigger migration from Migration Console, show sandbox validation, view generated diff), 6) Live Demo Part 3 (7:00-8:30, show Draft PR format, explain safety invariants, show validation logs), 7) Tech Stack & Testing (8:30-9:30, show pytest output, discuss Neon Postgres, Gemini LLM), 8) Closing (9:30-10:00, GitHub repo link, call to action). Include exact terminal commands to run, URLs to navigate, and specific UI elements to highlight.

Create docs/public-tunnel-setup.md with step-by-step guide. Sections: 1) Prerequisites (macOS/Linux, backend running on :8000, frontend on :5173), 2) Install Cloudflared ('brew install cloudflared' for macOS, apt/yum for Linux), 3) Tunnel Backend ('cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000', note the public HTTPS URL), 4) Tunnel Frontend ('cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:5173' in separate terminal), 5) Configure VITE_API_URL (create apps/web/.env.local with VITE_API_URL=<backend-tunnel-url>, restart frontend), 6) Test End-to-End (open frontend tunnel URL in browser, verify Dashboard loads, check Network tab shows API calls to backend tunnel), 7) Troubleshooting (CORS issues: verify FastAPI CORSMiddleware allows all origins, tunnel drops: use --protocol http2, rate limits: mention cloudflared free tier limits). Include security note: tunnels are public HTTPS URLs, do not expose production secrets.

Create docs/live-demo-script.md as concise 5-minute script for technical reviews. Outline: 1) Start (0:00-0:30, open frontend, show Dashboard, explain 'This is the control plane for autonomous API maintenance'), 2) Repositories (0:30-1:00, click Repositories tab, show 8 connected repos, highlight demo-checkout TypeScript repo), 3) API Inventory (1:00-1:45, click Inventory tab, show 40+ discovered usages, filter by FakePay provider, click into specific usage showing file path and line number), 4) Changes (1:45-2:30, click Changes tab, show breaking changes detected from FakePay v1→v2, highlight ENDPOINT_RENAMED and FIELD_REQUIRED), 5) Migration (2:30-4:00, click Migration tab, click 'Run Autonomous Migration', watch sandbox pipeline execute in real-time, show green PASS status), 6) Review (4:00-4:45, show generated unified diff for 5 files, highlight Draft PR card with evidence and validation logs), 7) Close (4:45-5:00, emphasize safety: 'Draft PR only, human review required, zero auto-merge'). Mark each timestamp with [SHOW] or [SAY] tags for clear narration cues.

Create docs/pitch-deck.md as Markdown slide deck (use --- separators for slide breaks). 15 slides: 1) Title (project name, tagline, GitHub link), 2) The Problem (engineers spend 20+ hours per quarter on API migration toil, screenshot of complex migration PR), 3) The Vision (autonomous agent detects → analyzes → rewrites → validates → PRs), 4) How It Works (7-step pipeline diagram with icons), 5) Architecture (system diagram: FastAPI + Neon + Gemini + React), 6) Change Detection (OpenAPI AST diffing example, show ENDPOINT_RENAMED change), 7) Repository Discovery (4-tier scanner output table), 8) Impact Analysis (show file impact graph, affected call sites), 9) Migration Generation (deterministic recipe vs LLM fallback decision tree), 10) Sandbox Validation (isolated worktree diagram, build/test/contract checks), 11) Safety Invariants (Draft PR only, no auto-merge, validation gate), 12) Demo Metrics (8 repos, 40+ usages, 6 migrations, 88 tests), 13) Tech Stack (badges grid), 14) What's Next (future: multi-language support, AI recipe learning, Slack/PagerDuty integration), 15) Thank You (GitHub link, contact email, live demo URL). Use Markdown formatting: ## for slide titles, bullet lists, **bold** for emphasis, `code` for technical terms.

Enhance README.md: Add new section '## Demo Materials' after '## What Has Been Built'. Subsections: 1) 'Realistic Demo Data' (explain seed_realistic_demo.py populates 3 orgs, 8 repos, 40+ usages, 6 migrations), 2) 'Video Walkthrough' (link to docs/video-walkthrough-script.md, mention 10-minute deep dive), 3) 'Live Demo Script' (link to docs/live-demo-script.md, 5-minute technical review format), 4) 'Public Tunnel Setup' (link to docs/public-tunnel-setup.md, for remote demos), 5) 'Pitch Deck' (link to docs/pitch-deck.md, for stakeholder presentations). Add new section '## Repository Structure' showing directory tree with brief descriptions: apps/api (FastAPI backend), apps/web (React frontend), packages/ (7 analysis/migration packages), tests/ (pytest suite), scripts/ (demo runner, seeder), docs/ (demo materials).

Enhance README.md: Update '## Technology Stack' table to include Cloudflare Tunnels row (Layer: Networking & Tunneling, Technologies: Cloudflared, Description: Secure public HTTPS tunneling for live demos). Update '## Useful Commands' section: Add subsection 'F. Seed Realistic Demo Data' with command 'python3 -m scripts.seed_realistic_demo' and description 'Populates Neon Postgres with 3 orgs, 8 repos, 2 providers, 40+ usages, 6 migrations.' Add subsection 'G. Start Public Tunnel' with commands for backend and frontend tunnels.

Polish repository root: Create docs/ directory if it doesn't exist. Create docs/README.md as index: '# Demo Materials

This directory contains comprehensive demo documentation...' with links to all 4 documents. Verify all docs use consistent Markdown formatting (ATX headers ##, fenced code blocks with language tags, relative links). Add timestamp footer to each doc: 'Last updated: {date}'.

Create .github/README.md as GitHub-specific landing README (symlink or copy from root README.md). Add shields.io badges at top: build status (placeholder), test coverage (88 tests badge), license (MIT), database (Neon Postgres), AI (Google Gemini). Add 'Star this repo' CTA. Add 'Quick Start' section with 3 commands: git clone, pip install, uvicorn. Add 'Live Demo' section with placeholder for tunnel URL.
